source_row.item_data_json: {"options":{"A":"Review the complete medication regimen, including prescription drugs, OTC products, and supplements, for adverse effects, interactions, duplication, and management problems.","B":"Review only medications prescribed by the admitting clinician because drugs from other prescribers are outside the current medication review.","C":"Stop the oldest medications first because duration of therapy is the primary criterion for deprescribing in polypharmacy.","D":"Assume the regimen is safe when every drug was prescribed by a licensed clinician, even when several prescribers are involved."}}
source_row.rationale: The National Institute on Aging identifies polypharmacy as a particular concern in older adults. Taking many medicines can increase the risk of adverse reactions, drug interactions, and medication-management difficulties, making comprehensive review important.
source_row.source_detail: Polypharmacy/medication management: maintain and review a complete list because multiple medicines increase adverse-effect and interaction risk. source_row.stem: An older adult takes twelve medications prescribed by several clinicians. Which concern should the nurse prioritize during medication review?
